# Native TCPCI semantics fixtures, version 1

These are public, authored synthetic CI inputs and preserved legacy mechanics.
They are not real repository measurements, calibrated probabilities, scientific
performance evidence, or executable checkpoint state.

`source-preservation.json` pins 57 resources from public COLEMAN v4.20.0 at
`1edbee874129aa85e26e592d9649826e85e1ac6b`: 46 Python sources using the declared
non-docstring AST profile, and 11 exact `py.typed` markers. Full source hashes
remain recorded even when documentation changes independently of mechanisms.

`legacy-ci-inputs.json` declares four builds, three tests, seconds, binary
pass/fail and a modeled 50% time budget. Its contextual feature is an authored
signal, without a claim of historical point-in-time availability.

`legacy-dispatch.json` retains all 37 actual names, constructor configuration,
agent/window routes and the observed 34 completions/three factory failures.
The paired v4/current trace comparison was on CPython 3.14.6/macOS arm64 with
the recorded native pins. It does not promise identical Linux/BLAS floating
state or ties. FRRMAB had four distinct traces in four predetermined process
runs within each source revision; a single deterministic trace is explicitly
unqualified. No normalization or repeat-until-match was used.
The historical driver requested `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` but used Python `-I`, which
ignores that environment request. Its effective hash seed was not controlled by
the request. The fixture records this limitation explicitly; the immutable raw
capture is retained rather than rewritten as proof of controlled hash order.

`catalog-source-evidence.json` independently retains the baseline byte hashes
and file lengths used to check every policy, route and reward evidence pin.
`catalog-lookups.json` preserves all 37 semantic names, their explicit routes
and all six credit definitions without duplicating the complete catalog.

`exp3-decision.json`, `contextual-decision.json` and `window-decision.json` are
complete self-contained frozen-record codec goldens. `fixture-producer.json`
retains their authored configuration, input and producer declarations. These
records precede evaluation: sampling mass is not recorded and generic loss is
not defined. Their producer digest identifies the retained declaration, not an
authenticated installed runtime or supplier checkpoint.

The portable goldens retain exact canonical data. They do not imply that native
execution recomputes a universal numerical trace. New captures are separate
reviewed fixtures; old captures and their limitations remain immutable.
